newsitem.title: UK: Ivory & Sime sees full year profits down.
newsitem.headline: Ivory & Sime sees full year profits down.

text.p: Fund manager Ivory & Sime Plc said on Friday it expected a modest profit decline in the current financial year following a big drop in funds under management.

In a statement accompanying annual results Ivory & Sime chairman David Kinloch said a 25 percent fall in funds under management to 3.2 billion sterling would impact on revenues in the year to end-April 1998.
"This should be partly offset by anticipated lower selling expenses and higher revenues arising from business gained during the year," he said.
"On balance, therefore, we currently expect a modest reduction in the coming year's profit."
The group said pre-tax profits in the year to end-April came in at 6.89 million sterling from 6.53 million.
Kinloch said the group had successfully rebuilt and strengthened all of its fund management teams following a spate of resignations at the firm earlier this year.
The sharp decline in funds under management was the result of losing the management contract on BAA Plc's pension scheme -- a fund of some 460 million sterling.
The loss of the contract followed the spate of resignations of senior fund managers, followed by the resignation of managing director Colin Hook in February.
He said good one year performance figures announced last year were beginning to translate into good three year numbers in some areas.
